```{r}
here::i_am("dplyr-101.Rproj")

```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
data("diamonds")
```

## Link between diamond carat and price

```{r}
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x=carat, y=price)) +
  geom_point()
```

## Selecting a subset of a dataset

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds_2ct <- diamonds |>
  filter( abs(carat - 2) < 0.1)
```

```{r}
ggplot(diamonds_2ct, aes(x=carat, y=price)) +
  geom_point()
```

## Prices of 2 carat diamonds

```{r}
diamonds |>
  filter(carat >= 2, carat <= 2.1) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=carat,y=price, group=carat)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

## Prices of 2 carat diamonds

```{r}
diamonds |>
  filter(carat >= 2, carat <= 2.1) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=carat,y=price, group=carat)) +
  geom_violin()
```

## Using filter

::::: columns
::: column
Filter is used as follows

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
filter(dataframe,exp, exp2, exp3)
```

Interpretation: the code keeps rows of the data frame for which the expression evaluates to TRUE.
:::

::: column
```{r}
filter(diamonds, price == 1000, cut == "Ideal") |>
  ggplot(aes(y=color)) + geom_bar()
```
:::
:::::

# Logical expression

## Basic expression

Evertything that compares two values and returns `TRUE` or `FALSE`.

```{r}
x <- 2
x == 2
x >= 3
```

## Logical operators

Combining true value

```{r}
#| echo: true
TRUE & FALSE
TRUE | FALSE
!FALSE
```

## Examples

Two different filter operations:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
diamonds |> filter(price == 1000, cut == "Ideal")
diamonds |> filter((price == 1000) | (cut == "Ideal"))
```

# Introduction to summarise

## Global summaries

```{r}
diamonds |> summarise(mean(price), median(price))
```

summarise is used as follows:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
summaise(dataframe, expression based on an aggregatiom function)
```

The result is a data frame with one column per expression and one row.

## Aggregation functions

::::: columns
::: {.columns width="50%"}
An aggregation function computes a statistics(in a broad sense) on a numerical vector, for instance

- mean
- median
- sd : standard deviation
- var : variance
- max and min
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
x <- c(-0.1, 1, 2, 2, -3, 5)
mean(x)
sd(x)
min(x)
n_distinct(x)
length(x)
```
:::
:::::

## Limitations of summarise {.smaller}

Aggregation functions are mostly limited to numerical values (and l= to logical ines to some extend). Aggregation functions for non numerical vectors generally output multiple values.

```{r}
#| echo: true
y <- c("A", "A", "B", "C", "A", "C", "C", "D")
table(y)
```

```{r}
diamonds |> pull(cut) |> table()
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
diamonds |> summarise(table(cut))
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds |> summarise(mean_price = mean(price), median_price = median(price), interquartile_price = IQR(price))
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds|> summarise(median_price = median(price), .by = cut)
```

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds|> summarise(median_price = median(price), .by = cut)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
Effects of .by

1)  split the data frame into as many sub-data frames as values taken by the .by variable
2)  apply the aggregation functions to each sub-data
:::
:::::

## Manual calculation for one value

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds|> filter(cut == "Ideal") |>  summarise(median_price = median(price))
```

## Graphical investigation

```{r}
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x=price, colour = cut)) + geom_density(bw="sj", linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.75) +
geom_rug(alpha = 0.5)
```

## Additional statistics

```{r}
diamonds|> summarise(median = median(price),
                     mean = mean(price),
                     sd = sd(price),
                     IQR = IQR(price),
                     .by = cut) |> arrange(cut)
                    
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds|> summarise(count = n(), .by = cut)
```

## Dependencies

A stndard way to assess dependency between two nummerical variables is Pearson's correlations= coefficient: cor

```{r}
diamonds|> summarise(cor(carat, price))
```

```{r}
diamonds|> summarise(cor(carat, price), .by=cut)
```

## Dependencies (non numerical)

```{r}
diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x=cut, fill=color)) + geom_bar(position="fill")
```

```{r}
diamonds |> summarise(n(), .by=c(cut,color)) |> arrange(cut, color) |> slice(1:5)
```

# Operate on columns
## Introduction to mutate

The mutate verb is used to create new columns (or to monify existing ones) based on calculation conducted on existing columns. General form:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false 
mutate(dataframe, newcolumn = expression)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds_ppc <- diamonds |> mutate("price per carat" = price/carat)
```

```{r}
diamonds_ppc |> summarise(median(`price per carat`), .by=cut) |> arrange(cut)
```

```{r}
diamonds_ppc|> summarise(median = median(`price per carat`),
                     mean = mean(`price per carat`),
                     sd = sd(`price per carat`),
                     IQR = IQR(`price per carat`),
                     .by = cut) |> arrange(cut)
```
                    
## Global extreme diamonds
                 
```{r}
diamonds_ppc |>
  filter(`price per carat` > 10000) |>
slice(1:5) |>
  select(1:6)
```                
          

This selects diamonds with a price (per carat) larger than the average one +2 * sd(`price per carat`).

```{r}
diamonds_ppc |>
  filter(`price per carat` > mean(`price per carat`))
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x=price, colour = cut)) + geom_density(bw="sj", linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
geom_rug(alpha = 0.5)
```
```{r}
diamonds_with_stats <-
diamonds_ppc |>
  mutate(mean = mean(`price per carat`), sd = sd(`price per carat`), large_ppc = mean +2*sd)
```

```{r}
diamonds_with_cond_stats <-
diamonds_ppc |>
  mutate(mean = mean(`price per carat`), sd = sd(`price per carat`), large_ppc = mean +2*sd, .by = cut)
```

```{r}
diamonds_with_cond_stats |>
filter(`price per carat` > large_ppc) |>
ggplot(aes(x=`price per carat`, colour = cut)) + geom_density(bw="sj", linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.75) +
geom_rug(alpha = 0.5)
```
# Application to discrete data

## Visual conditional distributions

```{r}
diamonds |>
  ggplot(aes(x=cut, fill=color)) +
  geom_bar(position="fill")
```
# Conditional frequencies {.smaller}


::::: columns
:::(.column width="40%")
```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds_counts <-
  diamonds|>
  summarise(n(), .by=c(cut, color))
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds_cond_counts <-
diamonds_counts |> mutate(freq = `n()`/sum(`n()`), .by=cut)
```
:::

::: (.column width="60%")

```{r}
diamonds_cond_counts |>
  slice(1:5)
```
:::
:::::

# Slice

## Slice Principles

`filter` subsets 
`slice`

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds |>
  slice(2:6)
```

## Slice variations

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds |>
  slice(1, .by = cut)
```

## Max and min

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds |>
  slice_min(price)
```

## Grouped max/min {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds |>
  slice_max(carat, by = cut)
```
## Other slice functions
- slice_head : select rows  from the top of the data frame
- slice_tail : selects rows from the bottom of the data frame
- slice_sample : selects  random sample of the rows (uniform distributions without replace by default)

# Select

## Select Principles

The goal of the function is to select some of the variables in a data frame, based on the proprieties (position, name and content)

The basic use leverages names:

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds |> 
  slice_tail(n=5) |>
  select(carat, cut, price)
```

## Select with position

Select can use columns indexes in a similar way to slice.

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds |> 
  slice_max(carat, by = color)
  select(1:4, 7)
```

## Select by name proprieties

Select can operate by looking at conditions on the names.

```{r}
#| echo: true
diamonds |> 
  slice_max(carat, n = 5) |>
  select(starts_with("c"))
```
```{r}
#| message: false
library(readxl)
credit_default <- read_excel(here("data", "default of credit card clients.xls"), skip = 1)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
credit_default |> 
  slice_max(LIMIT_BAL, n = 5) |>
  select(starts_with("L"))
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
credit_default |> 
  slice_max(LIMIT_BAL) |>
  select(matches("PAY_[0-9]"))
```
